title: Enhancing Cybersecurity Awareness Given Recent Increase in Phishing Scams
what_it_is: Enhancing Cybersecurity Awareness Given Recent Increase in Phishing Scams

sections.label: WhatsApp phishing scam victims
sections.summary: A question cites at least 237 phishing victims since November 2023 losing at least $606,000, with scammers using compromised WhatsApp accounts to solicit money.

sentences.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs in light of the recent phishing scams involving at least 237 victims since November 2023 with total losses amounting to at least $606,000 as stated in the Police advisory of 13 November 2023, what specific measures are being taken to enhance cybersecurity awareness among the public, especially regarding the use of popular messaging platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: They had then scanned the QR code in the website via their WhatsApp account on their mobile device and, in doing so, they inadvertently granted the scammers access to their WhatsApp account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The scammers then used the compromised WhatsApp account to impersonate the user and reached out to the user's family and friends and convinced them to transfer monies to the scammers' bank accounts or PayNow numbers.

sections.label: Online Criminal Harms Act directions
sections.summary: The Online Criminal Harms Act, progressively operationalised from this quarter, lets the Government direct online messaging platforms to disable access to accounts suspected of scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Online Criminal Harms Act which will be progressively operationalised from this quarter, will allow the Government to direct online messaging platforms to disable access to accounts suspected to be involved in scams.

sections.label: SPF WhatsApp phishing advisories
sections.summary: For the recent spike in phishing scams compromising WhatsApp accounts, the SPF issued advisories urging the public to adopt the three steps Add, Check, Tell.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Specific to the recent spike in phishing scams involving compromise of WhatsApp accounts, the SPF had issued several advisories which urged members of the public to adopt the three simple steps of "Add", "Check", "Tell".

sections.label: Police working with Meta, Google
sections.summary: Police worked with Meta on compromised WhatsApp accounts and with platforms including Google on safeguards like pre-emptive detection and blocking of phishing URLs, and intend closer work with Meta.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In my response, I will attempt to take them together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I mentioned that the Police have been working with Meta to stop further abuse of compromised WhatsApp accounts and the Police have also been working with online platforms, including Google, to introduce safer safeguards, and I had specifically mentioned through the pre-emptive detection and blocking of URLs linked to phishing sites.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For example, Meta has, on some occasions, required more time to recover compromised WhatsApp accounts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We intend to work even closer with Meta and to highlight to them that we need them to do more.

sections.label: Scam variants and platform levers
sections.summary: Scam variants are highlighted to platforms for better search engine optimisation, and the Online Criminal Harms Act, in force first quarter of 2024, gives levers for Government directions and detection requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are highlighting these scam variants to them, so that they can take better care and look at how their search engines can be better optimised to prevent such scam variants from taking place on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: I mentioned also that the Online Criminal Harms Act will come into force in the first quarter of 2024.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We have various levers under the Online Criminal Harms Act which will allow the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Government to better work with these platforms to issue Government directions against scams and to also require designated providers to detect and minimise scams and other malicious cyber activities.
